title: The Pentagon Just Cleared Half a Billion Dollars to Keep India's Apaches and Howitzers Battle-Ready
excerpt: Two new support packages worth $482 million cover spare parts, training, and maintenance for American-made attack helicopters and artillery — the unsexy work that keeps a $20 billion defence relationship alive.
body:
The United States just cleared nearly half a billion dollars to keep India's American-made attack helicopters and artillery guns combat-ready. The paperwork is routine. The signal is not.

The Defense Security Cooperation Agency notified Congress of two proposed support packages totalling $482.2 million — $230 million for long-term sustainment of India's M777A2 Ultra-Light Howitzers and $198.2 million for follow-on support of its AH-64E Apache attack helicopters. An additional $54 million covers ancillary logistics. The notifications, published in the Federal Register on 17 June, were formally delivered to Congress last week.

## What the Money Buys

Neither package involves new weapons. Both cover the less glamorous essentials that keep advanced military platforms operational: spare parts, depot-level maintenance, training, field service representatives, technical publications, and repair-and-return services.

For equipment as complex as the Apache — arguably the world's most advanced attack helicopter, with millimetre-wave radar, Hellfire missiles, and a sensor suite that can identify targets through dust and darkness — and the M777 — a 4,200-kilogram titanium-and-aluminium howitzer engineered specifically for high-altitude, thin-air combat — this kind of sustained support is what separates a functioning military asset from an expensive decoration.

India operates 22 AH-64E Apaches, deployed with the Indian Air Force for precision-strike and battlefield reconnaissance. It also fields 145 M777A2 howitzers, many of them positioned along the Line of Actual Control with China in Ladakh and Arunachal Pradesh, where temperatures drop below minus 30 degrees Celsius and supply lines stretch across some of the highest passes on earth. Keeping these systems combat-ready in such conditions is not a luxury — it is a logistical challenge that demands constant investment.

The Pentagon was explicit in its justification. 'This proposed sale will support the foreign policy and national security objectives of the United States by helping to strengthen the US-Indian strategic relationship,' the agency said, adding that it would 'improve India's capability to meet current and future threats, strengthen its homeland defence, and deter regional threats.'

## The Contractors

Boeing and Lockheed Martin are the principal contractors for the Apache support package, operating from Arlington, Virginia, and Orlando, Florida, respectively. BAE Systems, based in Cumbria, UK, leads the M777 sustainment programme. The Pentagon noted that neither deal requires additional US government or contractor personnel to be stationed in India, and that there would be 'no adverse impact on US defence readiness.'

## From Zero to $20 Billion

The numbers tell a larger story. India-US defence trade was effectively zero in 2008. Today, cumulative bilateral defence deals exceed $20 billion. India now conducts more military exercises with the United States than with any other country, and the two nations have signed all four foundational defence agreements — covering logistics sharing, communications interoperability, geospatial cooperation, and industrial security.

This latest clearance follows a pattern of deepening defence ties under the 'Major Defence Partner' designation India received in 2016 — a status that gives it access to defence technology on par with America's closest allies. US Ambassador Sergio Gor, speaking at the USISPF Leadership Summit on 30 June, called India 'one of the United States' most trusted partners' and pointed to India's early inclusion in the PAXSilica initiative — a 35-nation semiconductor supply-chain pact — as evidence of that trust.

The timing is also notable. The $482 million clearance arrives as India and the US are in what Gor described as the 'last one per cent' of negotiations on a bilateral trade deal — a broader commercial agreement that the ambassador said would be 'incredibly useful' for businesses trading between the two countries.

## Why the Diaspora Should Watch

Defence deals of this kind rarely make headlines in the diaspora press. But they underpin the strategic relationship that shapes everything from visa policy to trade access. When the Pentagon tells Congress that India is 'an important force for political stability, peace, and economic progress in the Indo-Pacific,' it is making the institutional case that the US-India corridor matters — a case that benefits every Indian professional, student, and entrepreneur navigating the American system.

The M777 howitzers are deployed along India's northern borders in some of the world's most inhospitable terrain. The Apaches provide the Indian Air Force with precision-strike capability it previously lacked. Keeping both combat-ready is not just a military priority — it is a strategic vote of confidence that both governments are investing in a partnership built to last.
